speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have had a tympanoplasty and are now experiencing occasional shooting ear pain along with difficulty wearing earrings. To understand what might be causing this, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and how long it lasts?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your history of chronic ear infections, recent tympanoplasty, and the specific triggers of eating and pressure, could you describe the exact quality of the pain when you eat—is it a sharp, electric shock-like sensation, and does it radiate to your teeth or jaw?

REQUEST TEST: High-resolution CT Temporal Bone (to evaluate graft integrity and potential ossicular chain issues).

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT results are normal, which is reassuring, but your description of pain triggering while eating combined with difficulty wearing earrings is highly suggestive of a specific complication involving the facial nerve or myofascial issues. Can you tell me if you notice any twitching of your mouth, forehead, or cheek on the affected side when you eat or when the pressure from an earring touches your ear? Also, has anyone observed you clenching your jaw or having muscle spasms in your ear canal recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myofascial pain syndrome of the auricular muscles (tensor tympani/stapedius) with referred otalgia.
